title: Threat Profile Signature Clustering
description:
A network security system captures raw event logs, each represented as a string of lowercase English letters. Security analysts classify two event logs under the same "threat profile" if both strings contain the exact same frequency for every character, regardless of character order.

Given an array of strings `logs`, write an algorithm to group the logs that belong to the same threat profile signature together. The grouped threat profiles can be returned in any order, and the order of logs within a group does not matter.
constraints: logs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
output_format: A list of lists of strings, where each sublist represents a group of event logs with identical character frequency signatures.

examples.explanation: The logs "apt", "tap", and "pat" all contain one 'a', one 'p', and one 't'. The logs "net" and "ten" contain one 'e', one 'n', and one 't'. "bot" forms its own group.
An empty string log is grouped by itself.
Duplicate logs share the exact same character counts and belong to the same group.
